# Independent audit: exposed simplex-face atomic descent

Source: `candidate 0946668727a45f68`, Sections 1–6. Verdict: **PASS** under its explicit whole-minimal-face atomic-payment and unpenalized bad-level premises.

The selected faces are proper since their common mass Q is below M. Equal positive face masses make distinct selected faces an antichain. A same-parity pair of relative-interior deepest witnesses has an actual deepest midpoint; its minimal face is the face join and strictly contains either selected face. That contradicts its required mass Q. Thus there are at most k selected faces, and their union mass is at most kQ<Gamma_d M<M, with overlaps counted only once.

The simultaneous contraction is genuinely compatible. A target inside a selected exposed face can only be represented by input bases from that face. Chosen interior centers at its simplex vertices interpolate affinely; adjacent simplex faces have the same vertex values on their common face, so the centers agree on every overlap. Hence every input to a modified target is contracted at the same rate about compatible affine centers. Targets outside the union are unchanged and all changed inputs are nested subsets. This proves exact sampled-fiber compatibility, including representations involving face-boundary bases.

Each selected face is isolated by a pure-base cap of new mass rQ. The outside bases retain their old strict maximum gap by the stated positive-fiber uniform continuity. Updating the actual mass, covariance, energy, and the continuous scalar geometric-mean normalization therefore still yields Q(t)<=rQ. Since the union has mass less than M, the displayed ratio decreases strictly. No original mark is presumed deepest along the deformation.

The three-interval obstruction correctly separates closed minors from faces: shrinking only {0,1} would require 1+r<=2r, impossible for r<1 even after arbitrary translations. A closed minor controls representations made FROM its points; it does not control all representations TARGETING it. The theorem and final scope paragraphs preserve this distinction, and do not cover interior atomic bottlenecks or mixed atomic/proper groups.
